correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the fourteen labelled Fano point/line incidence graph from seven triples (21 edges), the synchronous open-neighbor majority rule and tie retention on deleted degree-two vertices. Independently wrote, compiled, and executed a full-domain bitmask C++ checker without executing the submitted program. It enumerated all 232 choices and every one of 16384 labelled binary states each (3,801,088 graph-states), followed each trajectory to first period one or two, compared basin membership bitwise, checked exact fixed and primitive two-cycle counts, and checked every pair class. Results intact=(58,1653,2592,0,0,2), one=(66,777,3744,1152,0,6), adjacent two=(58,533,4960,2368,0,11), disjoint cross=(90,376,4032,1736,296,8), disjoint no-cross=(86,427,4512,2048,128,6), where tuple is (fixed,two-cycles,consensus,gained,lost,max-entry). This directly certifies the exact finite 232-graph domain and the sharp adjacent/disjoint threshold; no finite-to-infinite inference is asserted.

value.rationale: A sharp graph-specific robustness threshold for a canonical finite incidence geometry is mathematically motivated: distinguishes basin cardinality gains from actual basin inclusion, gives smallest destructive number of deletions, complete 232-case structural partition and a sharp 11-iteration clock. The exact invariant is not a routine textbook consequence of period-at-most-two or the intact graph projection. Limitation: entirely a fixed 14-vertex graph and finite exhaustive theorem, no extrapolation to larger projective planes.

limitations: Definition uses incumbent tie retention; only zero, one or two incidence deletions on one labelled Fano graph. Prior 58-symbol intact projection credited.
